claude.sample_unit: chatbot recipients (6505 birthing individuals and 7489 newborn caregivers)

links.outcome: Chatbot reach (opening) by race, insurance, prenatal care location
links.effect: Lower postpartum reach for Black (OR 0.73) vs White, public insurance (OR 0.72) vs private; newborn reach lower for Black (OR 0.61), public insurance (OR 0.63), FQHC prenatal care (OR 0.50)
links.quote: The odds of opening the postpartum chatbot were significantly lower for individuals identified in the EHR as Black (odds ratio [OR] 0.73, 95% CI 0.61- 0.88) compared to White individuals.

links.outcome: Chatbot reach before vs after feedback-based content and outreach revision
links.effect: No change after revision: postpartum 64.1% to 62.8% (OR 0.95, 0.85-1.05); newborn 65.9% to 65.2% (OR 0.97, 0.88-1.07); Spanish version improved newborn reach 58% to 66.2% (OR 1.42)
links.quote: No significant changes in reach were found after launching the updated version of the newborn and postpartum outreach and chatbot content, nor after including the chatbot information in patients’ discharge paperwork ( Table 5 ); thus, we focused on results in the combined analyses for the full time period.

unlisted_practices: Professionally translated Spanish-language version of patient-facing chatbot to increase reach among Spanish-preferring patients
Adding chatbot information and screenshots to discharge paperwork to raise awareness and address scam concerns

openai.sample_unit: chatbot-recipient records: 6505 postpartum and 7489 newborn; recipients overlap
models_evaluated: Rule-based postpartum chatbot with fixed interaction logic
Rule-based newborn caregiver chatbot with fixed interaction logic

links.outcome: Differences in chatbot reach by race
links.effect: Black versus White individuals had lower postpartum chatbot reach: OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.61- 0.88; newborn chatbot reach: OR 0.61, 95% CI 0.50-0.74.
links.quote: The odds of opening the postpartum chatbot were significantly lower for individuals identified in the EHR as Black (odds ratio [OR] 0.73, 95% CI 0.61- 0.88) compared to White individuals.

links.effect: Content revisions did not improve reach: postpartum OR 0.95 (95% CI 0.85-1.05); newborn OR 0.97 (95% CI 0.88-1.07). Spanish-language newborn reach improved from 58% to 66.2%.
links.quote: Including a Spanish-language version in the newborn chatbot improved reach among Spanish-preferring caregivers (from 58% to 66.2%), but additional chatbot content revision and the addition of chatbot information to discharge paperwork did not change chatbot reach.

links.outcome: Chatbot reach after adding chatbot information to discharge paperwork
links.effect: Postpartum reach changed from 63.6% to 63.9% (OR 1.02, 95% CI 0.90-1.15); newborn reach changed from 66.2% to 64.6% (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.83-1.05). Neither change was significant.
links.quote: No significant changes in reach were found after launching the updated version of the newborn and postpartum outreach and chatbot content, nor after including the chatbot information in patients’ discharge paperwork ( Table 5 ); thus, we focused on results in the combined analyses for the full time period.

unlisted_practices: Provide professionally translated chatbot content and language-switching instructions in patients’ preferred language; Spanish translation improved newborn chatbot reach but not postpartum chatbot reach.

models_evaluated: Safe Babies Safe Moms postpartum and newborn chatbots

links.effect: Black patients and those with public insurance had significantly lower odds of opening the chatbots than White patients and those with private insurance.
links.quote: We found notable differences in chatbot reach by age, race, insurance type, and prenatal care location for both chatbots.

links.effect: Refining outreach messages and chatbot content based on user feedback did not significantly improve the overall reach of the newborn or postpartum chatbots.
links.quote: No significant changes in reach were found after launching the updated version of the newborn and postpartum outreach and chatbot content, nor after including the chatbot information in patients’ discharge paperwork ( Table 5 ); thus, we focused on results in the combined analyses for the full time period.

unlisted_practices: Translating patient-facing chatbot content into users' preferred languages (e.g., Spanish) to improve reach among linguistically diverse subgroups
